title: Insurer's internal AI assistant and claims data lake

organisation.name: Meridale Mutual
organisation.size: 1,900 staff; claims, underwriting and data science teams
organisation.summary: Meridale Mutual gives employees an internal AI assistant for claims work. Questions go to a claims agent that retrieves passages from a vector store fed nightly from the company document shares, calls the model through an LLM gateway, and can use three tools: a claims lookup in the data lake, the ticketing system and the claims mailbox. Claim documents that arrive by email are filed to the shares automatically. Analysts query the claims data lake from notebooks, and prompts and tool definitions are deployed by a prompt and model CI pipeline.

ai_llm_security.summary: A claimant's document carries instructions the agent follows when it is retrieved
Retrieved text tells the agent to email claim details to an outside address

data_security.summary: HR files were indexed without their access lists, so anyone can retrieve them
Analysts export claims with health data from notebooks to personal storage

cloud_security.summary: The agent's cloud role can query the whole claims data lake
Notebook sessions hold long-lived cloud credentials for the data lake

devsecops_supply_chain.summary: A prompt or tool definition change ships to production without review
A dependency of the agent's tool code is replaced upstream

identity_access.summary: The agent calls tools with its own rights, not the asking employee's
A stolen SSO session gives an outsider the assistant and its tools

threat_intelligence.summary: A report on attackers planting instructions in documents sent to insurers
Intelligence on a fraud ring testing claim stories against insurers' assistants

incident_response.summary: The email log shows claim details sent to free-mail addresses by the agent
A poisoned document is in the vector store and the agent keeps retrieving it

grc_risk.summary: Health details in claims reach an outside LLM provider without a documented basis
No policy says what the agent may do without a person

api_security.summary: The claims lookup tool's API takes any claim id with the agent's token
The gateway's provider key is shared by every app and can be used directly

application_security.summary: The chat app renders model output as HTML, so an image link leaks the conversation
Ticket text written by the agent is rendered unescaped in the ticketing UI

endpoint_security.summary: An infostealer on a laptop takes the assistant's SSO session
A malicious macro on a laptop writes documents into the shares that feed the assistant

reviewNotes: Intermediate: outside email becomes retrievable text (indirect injection); the agent acts with its own broad rights; ACLs were lost at ingestion; nothing logs tool arguments.
